### Watch screen (`cdpm watch`)
- See the tabs of all running slots live on one page: `cdpm watch` (all), `cdpm watch 1 2` (chosen slots), `--cols N` (tiles per row, 1–8, default 4), `--port N` (default 14900), `cdpm watch --stop`. Or just ask Claude to "open the watch screen". No new MCP tools: it is a small separate web server.
- Each slot gets a row with its seven-segment slot number; tabs are equal-size tiles. Click a tile to see it large in place. A ★ marks the tab in front of each window (moves within ~0.2 s when you switch tabs).
- Actions apply directly, without the AI: × on a tile closes the tab; right-click for reload, back, bring to front, copy URL, move to another slot; right-click a slot number to pause/resume, open a new tab or close the whole slot (confirmed, and it waits until the browser processes are gone). Agents get a slot message about what the user did.
- Drag a tile onto another slot to move the tab: the receiving slot opens the same address, and the original tab closes once the new one exists. Logins and storage are not copied (each slot keeps its own profile; sites like Google bind sessions to the browser, so copying cookies doesn't carry the login and can sign the original out). Moving a slot's last tab leaves a blank tab so that browser stays up. A dashed preview shows where the tab will land.
- Side panel: messages agents send each other, newest first (last 100).
- Light/dark theme toggle; columns and theme are remembered per browser.
- Not visible to sites: the front tab streams what Chrome already paints; background tabs are not kept rendering, only captured when first seen, when their address/title changes or an agent acts on them, plus follow-ups at 3, 10 and 30 s (background tabs paint late). Visibility is read from an isolated world (measured: 0 reads visible to the page).
- Local only (127.0.0.1), per-run token, foreign Host headers refused. Stays up while any slot runs; exits after 10 idle minutes with no slots and no viewers. Attaches to nothing while nobody is watching. Several watch pages can be open at once.

### Detection and telemetry signals
- From traffic CDPM already records (request URLs, response headers, *names* of cookies sent; never values), CDPM recognizes 117 vendors: 34 bot-detection/fingerprinting/fraud (Akamai, Cloudflare, Kasada, DataDome, PerimeterX, reCAPTCHA, …), 22 session-recording (Hotjar, Clarity, Contentsquare, …), 61 analytics/ads/error reporting (including Korean ones such as Naver and Kakao logging).
- When a page runs bot detection or session recording, or a page load is blocked/challenged (403/429 with a vendor's marks), the next tool result carries one `[signal]` line per site and vendor, and Claude tells the user in one line. Report only: nothing is blocked unless the user asks.
- `browser_network` with `telemetry: true` returns the breakdown per category (requests, bytes sent, hosts, evidence), including unnamed collection endpoints grouped by path.
- Cost: ~1 µs per request; nothing is injected into pages and no extra CDP commands are sent.

### Request blocking (`browser_block`)
- `signals` blocks by vendor name ("Hotjar") or category (`replay`, `analytics`, `bot`, `other`). Used only when the user asks.
- `quiet: true` answers matching requests with an empty success (204 / empty body / 1×1 image) instead of failing them, so the page doesn't notice.
- SharedWorker requests are now blocked too (they used to leak). Verified paths: page requests, beacons (including on unload), cross-site iframes, dedicated/shared/service workers, EventSource, prefetch. WebSocket cannot be blocked over CDP (it would need code injected into the page, which CDPM doesn't do).
- Vendor rules never block the site you are on or its own requests.
- Requests blocked by the browser itself (e.g. Brave Shields) or an extension are labelled as such, not as CDPM blocks.

### Other Chromium browsers
- Chrome by default; another Chromium browser per slot only when the user asks: `browser` on `browser_launch`, or `cdpm launch 2 --browser brave` (`brave`, `edge`, `chromium`, `vivaldi`). `cdpm browser` lists what is installed.
- Slots can mix browsers and versions; each browser has its own profile per slot. Taskbar/Dock slot icons, downloads and the watch screen work the same for all; the restart-after-Chrome-update check applies to Chrome slots only.

### Other
- Fixed slot icons flipping between old and new designs when several Claude Code windows ran different CDPM versions after an update. A CDPM process now leaves icons alone once the installed version differs from the one it runs, and shows a one-time note to reconnect. Sessions still on 0.1.19 or older need one reconnect (`/mcp`).
- Releases now also create the GitHub release page and update the MCP registry from the same GitHub Actions run.
- Auto-setup version 19 adds the watch-screen tip, the Chrome default and the report-only `[signal]` rule to existing installs.
- Tests: 85 unit, 60 integration (3 watch-screen and 4 request-blocking integration tests added). Also checked by hand on Windows (wide monitor) and macOS.
